Daniel Cox
Chartering Manager, Western Bulk
To, to explain those of you who are new, to, to Western Bulk, basic, basics of our business model. It is about providing our customers an efficient transport solution, but also managing their risk. What we do as an asset-light dry bulk operator is to match vessels and cargoes. The agenda for today, first, we'll talk through the 2025 performance. We'll move on to strategy and a bit on positioning, and then, round off with the market outlook. The indexes. The Supramax index increased from the summer lows of 10,000, 12,000, up to, to close to 19,000 by, by, by the autumn. That showed us that the market has a relatively tight utilization rate.
After a brief seasonal dip in December, the rates rebounded quickly, and we have gotten a pretty strong start to 2026. Also, the FFA market indicates a belief in the market for 2026, trading at relatively healthy levels. Looking at the basin spread, we could see for most of last year that it was trading within range. The difference or the spread between the Atlantic market and the Pacific markets. Q3 Atlantic was trading a bit in the upper range, and Q4 a bit in the lower range, but overall, it was relatively normal year when it comes to the basin spreads, which we are tracking quite closely.
This year, though, we can see, you can see the thick blue line on the graph to the right. You can see that we have broken out of trend, and this is very much in favor of the Atlantic market, which is trading at really strong levels for this time of the year, driven mainly by grains out of US Gulf and East Coast South America. That's quite noteworthy. 2025 was a year with improved results, but also focus on delivering on the strategy. As you can see from the key figures, the Net TC ended at $27.7 million. Second half, up from $9.3 million in 2024 to $20.1 million in 2025.
We were well-positioned to benefit from the dry bulk market upturn in the early second half. The admin expenses came in around $22 million, which is a reduction of $4.5 million from 2024, also in line with the previously communicated figures. Net profit, $5.44 million. Second half, up from -$4.6 in 2024 to $7.8 in 2025. An average of 110 vessels with a Net TC margin of close to $700 per day. We can see, we are progressing. We believe some of the initiatives that we have ongoing to improve the operating business is slowly starting to work. More about that on the next slides.
Strong liquidity and book equity with available liquidity, $65 million, free cash, $30 million, undrawn bank facilities totaling $35 million. Working capital requirements, $10 to 15 million, mainly driven by accounts receivables and bunker stocks. The book equity, almost $51 million. Plenty of ammunition to use as we go into 2026, looking for new opportunities, whether it being on the asset side, co-investing, people, other initiatives, tech, things that we believe can enhance the margins of Western Bulk going forward. Strategy, broadly put into two categories: strengthening and grow our core trading business, less dependent on market cycles. Scale a fleet of partnership-owned vessels, commercially managed by Western Bulk. This is to bring additional revenues and synergies to the trading business.
It's all about really strengthening the platform in as many ways as we can. Looking a bit more into the first point, improving the core trading.... We are of the strong belief that it's about the people. We need to retain the best people at Western Bulk. We need to develop the employees, all the employees we have. And we need to build and continue to build a performance culture and a winning mentality. It's tough competition in the operating space, still, and it will be for years to come. Only the strongest will really do well. Also data, improve the data we have, but we also need to have a culture where our chartering managers, our operations managers, and everybody in the organization also are curious about using data and see how we can become better by using data.
Attract complementary skills and networks to the platform. We have gone through the whole organization to see what's our strengths and where can we become stronger. We are humble to say that there is obviously some of our competitors out there that are doing stuff, making money on things that we don't do today. Some of those trades are very interesting, niche trades with a slightly higher base margin, which requires certain skills and network. We want to attract more of those individuals, teams, skill sets, and competency into our platform and build on that, and want that to be complementary to the bulk business that we are doing today, and all the excellent traders, operators, and people that we have doing bulk business in the company today.
So that's on improving the core trading, mainly about people and culture. Assets and commercial management, we want to co-invest. We rather own 10 ships, 20%, than to own two ships 100%. We wanna build something, we wanna build a service, we wanna show our partners that we are creating good value for them. By gaining access to Western Bulk platform, we wanna show them what that means and how well they will be taken care of. That's the way we want to invest, and also co-investing over time, we think it's a more sustainable business model. It's something that will give you a decent average price over the cycle. It's something that will spread your risk over the, over time.
There's plenty of reasons for us to like that way of thinking. Commercial management is a bit of add-on in terms of, but it's a similar thing, similar thinking. We want to open up the platform of Western Bulk and invite selected partners in to work together with us to maximize the return on their assets. That is that on this slide. Can take a little moment to sort of also pause and if there is any questions from the people here, since this is a bit of a new angle. All right. There will be a chance in the end to ask questions after the presentation as well.
Here we show an example around a practical example of how we are thinking as to complementary skills and networks. We brought in an experienced lumber and projects team of three individuals based in Bergen. They were commencing operations from 1 May 2026, and they have extensive experience in the niche trade and break bulk in general. That's a way for us to build. I think also just making sure that we integrate new people, new teams into the culture.
We will spend a lot of time on the due diligence part, having numerous, numerous, chats with, with the various people involved on, on, on, to making sure that there's a best possible chance of a good cultural fit as well. We are not rushing this. We wanna do things step by step. Yep. Another example is increasing the, the, the focus on the handy business we are doing in, in Asia. We hired Dan Cox to set up a small office in Sydney. 20 years of, of, of handy experience. We were lacking handy experience in Pacific, something we identified, a gap that we have now plugged, and we will build around it.
Sort of build activity around, and him and team out there. Practical example, again, this time from co-investing. We bought Kamsarmax, as some of you might know, together with three great Norwegian partners, where we took a 22% ownership stake, and we are responsible for the co-commercial management and business management in the project. That's ensuring the partners, obviously, access to customers and supplier networks, chartering and operational expertise, and also a broad range of in-house support functions. This was sort of an important milestone for us to set the structure and get it up and running, and from here, we hope to build on that.
One thing to mention there, though, is obviously the asset prices are steaming hot at the moment. We are having a lot of discussions around that, and we are now just gonna, you know, we're gonna weight our investments carefully. Also, that will depend. It will also be an important factor for the pace of how fast we can grow this new leg to stand on. It will also be market dependent. We're not just blindly gonna go out and execute on it without taking the market into consideration, obviously. Yes, that brings us to the market view.
As we have been saying for some time, we are relatively positive for the market in 2026, mainly based on the ton-mile story we see from the larger sizes, from Capesize and the trickle-down effect we can expect to see on the Kamsarmaxes and, again, the Ultramaxes. Also, we think we see an underlying high utilization rate in the dry bulk market, and it does not take much for the market to spike. There's just a bit of inefficiency coming in from either there is geopolitical shocks or other things that leads to sudden spikes in the market. I think it's a dangerous market to, over time, sit short in.
That being said, we will obviously be agile and at our usual selves when it come to changing our positions quickly around when we have a view. A bit cautious that things have already moved up quite fast. So we're already up to relatively high levels. Also worth mentioning, the underlying order book is still somewhat high on Ultramaxes. And also keeping in mind that we, as a company, tend to use Q1 to position ourselves for the remainder of the year. That sums up our presentation for today.
As normal, we try to we, we, we keep it rather brief, but fully open for, for questions now, if there is anything on your, your mind. Okay. Thank you very much for the presentation, and I wish you a great week ahead.
